method: Agent-curated claims from fetched official vendor pages. Confidence concerns published evidence, not authenticated feature testing or independent security assurance. NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED means not established in the reviewed sources, never feature absence.

vendors.name: Accredible
vendors.summary: Accredible documents digital credentials, programme engagement, pathways, a wallet and Job Market Insights. Its January 2026 announcement explicitly adds OB3 and W3C VC export and ingestion.
vendors.buyer_checks: Evaluate credential export and ingestion, pathway completion/dropoff reporting, and the source and scope of Job Market Insights. Confirm receiving-system compatibility rather than assuming that a standards label proves every exchange.

ICP: Universities, associations, product certification providers, employee training and awarding/testing bodies are listed audiences.
Positioning: A unified credential platform covering issuance, learning pathways, learner visibility and programme measurement.
Credentialing: Design and issue digital certificates and badges; editing, expiry and renewals are documented.
Digital Badges: Digital badge design and issuance with achievement, criteria and skills information.
Open Badges: Vendor announces OB2/OB3 conversion at sharing or verification, with OB3 export and ingestion.
W3C VC: January 13, 2026 announcement documents W3C VC export and ingestion. Confirm the exact model version, proof and receiver requirements.
CLR: Pathways and a wallet do not establish a CLR 2.0 implementation or certification role.
Skills: Credential skills and learning outcomes are linked to Job Market Insights.
Learner Records: A digital wallet and visual milestone learning pathways are documented; this is not evidence of CLR conformance.
Workforce Intelligence: Job Market Insights tied to programme skills and learning outcomes are documented. Exact dataset coverage, licensing and refresh are NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED in reviewed sources.
Verification: Verifiable credentials and conversion into supported open formats at sharing or verification are described.
Analytics: Email and credential engagement, social shares, referrals, pathway completions and dropoffs.
API: Pricing lists API access and exportable insights data; the platform links public API documentation. Confirm plan entitlements.
Integrations: Published integration directory and plan matrix list LMS/workflow connections including Moodle, Canvas and Zapier. Verify each connector and plan.
Security: Trust centre offers SOC 2 Type 2 report access, a bridge letter and a public SOC 3 summary. Current report period and contractual scope require review.
Data Residency: Operations documentation describes an opt-in EU region in Frankfurt at account creation, with region-specific backups. Confirm the full processing and transfer scope.
Pricing: Recipient-based plans; Launch displays $45/month on a 12-month term billed monthly, and custom plans are available. Recheck quota and inclusions at purchase.
Contract: Pricing FAQ states one-year and multi-year contracts; the displayed Launch offer is a 12-month term.
Higher Education: An official higher-education solution is listed, with university implementations on the platform page.
Enterprise: Custom recipient volumes, expanded features, enterprise security support and custom SLAs/terms are listed.
Certification Bodies: Product certification, associations and awarding/testing bodies are official solution categories.
Workforce Use Cases: Employee training, career-related credentials, learning pathways and Job Market Insights.

vendors.name: Certifier
vendors.summary: Certifier documents certificate and badge issuance, OB3, API and automation workflows, and enterprise controls. Its security hub publishes ISO certifications and European AWS hosting.
vendors.buyer_checks: Match annual issuance limits and billing to your programme. Test an OB3 export, the actual CRM/LMS workflow, roles, audit logs and SSO. Do not equate ISO certification with a SOC 2 report.

ICP: Organizations running certification programmes, including small teams and enterprise credential issuers.
Positioning: Digital certificate and badge issuance with branded delivery and enterprise credential workflows.
Credentialing: Design, generate, send, manage and verify digital certificates and badges.
Digital Badges: Vendor documents digital badge issuance and automatic OB3 compliance for issued badges.
Open Badges: Official OB3 guide states that issued badges support Open Badges 3.0 and claims 1EdTech certification. Exact registry role and sample export should be checked.
W3C VC: OB3's VC-based model is not separate evidence of standalone VC profiles, model versions or wallet presentation support.
CLR: Learning pathway creation does not establish CLR 2.0 conformance.
Skills: Skills are listed in the credential design feature matrix. Automatic taxonomy mapping is NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED.
Learner Records: Learning pathway creation is listed; a standards-based aggregate learner-record profile is NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED.
Workforce Intelligence: No comparable labour-market dataset, licensing, coverage or refresh was established.
Verification: OB3 guide describes badge metadata, a unique identifier and verification; test a real export and status lifecycle.
Analytics: Advanced analytics is listed in paid-plan and enterprise features; confirm metrics and plan access.
API: Pricing lists API access and documentation; legal terms define API access and its agreement/order conditions.
Integrations: Pricing and enterprise documentation list automation connections, including Zapier, Make and Pipedream, with tailored integrations at enterprise level.
Security: Security hub states ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 certification and GDPR practices; explicitly says it has no separate SOC 2 compliance report. Request current certificate scope.
Data Residency: Security hub states infrastructure is hosted on AWS within Europe. This alone does not establish EU-only processing or a selectable worldwide residency guarantee.
Pricing: Public free and paid tiers with annual issuing limits, billing choices and custom Enterprise pricing. Values vary with selected volume and billing; obtain a like-for-like quote.
Contract: Terms define monthly/multiple-month or annual subscription periods and a minimum obligation for each subscription term; API terms may depend on the agreement/order.
Higher Education: Enterprise product article explicitly discusses university continuing education and microcredential workflows.
Enterprise: Enterprise page lists SAML SSO, audit logs, custom DPA/SLA, roles, white-labeling and tailored integrations.
Certification Bodies: Enterprise article documents membership, partner and customer certification workflows; confirm the professional body's specific approval and renewal requirements.
Workforce Use Cases: Enterprise and partner training/certification issuance workflows; a labour-market intelligence product is not established by these use cases.

vendors.name: Credly
vendors.summary: Credly by Pearson documents Acclaim credential programmes, skills-oriented enterprise use cases, analytics and integrations. Its OB3 page specifically documents import and verification of OB2/OB3 badges from other issuers.
vendors.buyer_checks: Distinguish external badge import/verification from your own issuance profile. Test the contracted API, skills data feed, earner experience and integrations. Obtain the exact security and geographic processing terms.

ICP: Training providers, higher education, professional associations, product certification providers and enterprise organizations.
Positioning: Digital credential programmes and trusted skills intelligence within Pearson Workforce Skills.
Credentialing: Create, manage, market, analyze and scale digital credential programmes.
Digital Badges: Badge issuance and programme tracking are explicitly documented.
Open Badges: OB3 product page documents upload and verification of external OB2/OB3 badges with automatically parsed metadata. Do not infer universal OB3 issuance from this import feature.
W3C VC: The reviewed OB3 import page does not establish a standalone VC issuance or presentation profile.
CLR: A unified badge collection is not proof of CLR 2.0 conformance.
Skills: Credential metadata represents skills; enterprise positioning includes workforce capabilities and skills-based talent decisions.
Learner Records: Earners can combine imported badges from multiple issuers into a collection with verification. Exact CLR profile is NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED.
Workforce Intelligence: Enterprise skills intelligence and talent decisions are documented; OB3 imports enrich a Workforce API feed. Equivalent job-market coverage and refresh are NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED.
Verification: External OB2/OB3 badge verification and metadata parsing are documented; receiver and issuer-resource requirements still matter.
Analytics: Credential usage and earner engagement analytics, trends and programme optimization.
API: Official developer gateway links API fundamentals, authentication, endpoints and terms; OB3 page also describes a Workforce API.
Integrations: Acclaim page lists integrations including Canvas, Degreed and Zapier; confirm specific connector availability.
Security: Security page publishes ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 assurances and GDPR practices, with further security documentation on request. Current certificate validity and scope need review.
Data Residency: The reviewed security page does not establish selectable hosting regions or universal data-residency guarantees.
Pricing: Official pricing page directs organizations to request pricing for the selected solution; no universal public rate is supplied.
Contract: Pricing is sales-led; minimum term, renewals and enterprise license conditions require the actual contract.
Higher Education: Higher education institutions are explicitly addressed on the Acclaim product page.
Enterprise: Enterprise organizations are an explicit audience, with skills intelligence, internal mobility and talent decision use cases.
Certification Bodies: Professional associations and product certification providers are explicit product audiences.
Workforce Use Cases: Employee recognition, workforce capabilities, internal mobility and skills-based talent decisions.

vendors.name: Parchment
vendors.summary: Parchment documents an education records ecosystem spanning transcripts, diplomas, certificates, badges and CLRs. It also explicitly markets OB3-compliant badges for workforce programmes.
vendors.buyer_checks: Evaluate official transcript and diploma exchange separately from badge issuance. Ask how CLR data is structured and exchanged, which SIS/LMS/API connections apply, and which regional agreement governs storage and international transfers.

ICP: Education institutions and learners, plus employers and training organizations using workforce credentials.
Positioning: An education credential and records platform connecting transcripts, diplomas, badges, certificates and CLRs.
Credentialing: Official records issuance and exchange, including transcripts, diplomas, certificates, badges and CLRs.
Digital Badges: Higher-education and workforce digital badge products are documented.
Open Badges: Workforce product page explicitly describes OB3-compliant, metadata-rich digital badges.
W3C VC: OB3 and CLR product labels do not establish every standalone VC profile, proof suite or wallet presentation.
CLR: Dedicated CLR Services include record planning, structuring, sharing and consulting. Confirm the exact CLR standard version and registry role.
Skills: Badges validate skills; CLR Services describe skills and competencies within wider institutional learning evidence.
Learner Records: Transcripts, diplomas and CLR Services connect academic and co-curricular achievements.
Workforce Intelligence: Workforce badges, pathways and CLR career connections are described. A comparable labour-market dataset, licensing and refresh are NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED.
Verification: Official credential exchange and verifiable OB3 badges are described; test the actual issuer/status/receiver workflow.
Analytics: Higher-education badge analytics and workforce programme reporting/real-time analytics are documented.
API: Public material reviewed does not establish a self-serve API contract; this is not a claim that APIs are unavailable.
Integrations: Connections between badges, official records, learning pathways and CLR services are described. Exact SIS/LMS connector and entitlement list is NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED in the reviewed pages.
Security: Trust page states annual SOC 2 Type II auditing, encryption, access controls and security-report access. Review the actual current report and contracted product scope.
Data Residency: Published DPA states US storage and authorizes processing/transfers in the US or other subprocessor countries. Confirm applicable regional terms; do not interpret this as a universal US-only guarantee.
Pricing: Institutional get-a-quote page; request product-specific pricing and clarify institution versus learner ordering charges.
Contract: Quote-led institutional procurement; minimum license term and renewal terms are NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED. A public DPA addresses processing obligations, not a universal product price.
Higher Education: Dedicated higher-education badge and CLR products, in addition to official academic records.
Enterprise: Workforce programmes address training providers and employers; specific enterprise license/SLA details are NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED.
Certification Bodies: Employer/training use cases alone do not establish a dedicated professional-body certification/renewal product.
Workforce Use Cases: Skills recognition across employee learning, training credentials, career pathways and workforce programme reporting.

vendors.name: Sertifier
vendors.summary: Sertifier documents enterprise credential workflows, Open Badges, W3C VCs, API/webhooks, configurable EU/US residency and a dedicated CLR product. These are shared capabilities to evaluate, not grounds for declaring CertifyMe uniquely broader.
vendors.buyer_checks: Test the exact Open Badges version, VC export/proof and CLR profile rather than relying on broad standards wording. Confirm residency across backups/subprocessors and obtain the applicable security assurance and enterprise SLA.

ICP: Enterprise learning, partner/customer certification, training providers and institutions using CLRs.
Positioning: Design, issue and verify credentials across employee learning, partner certification and customer education.
Credentialing: Branded digital certificates and badges with automated training completion workflows.
Digital Badges: Enterprise page explicitly describes digital certificates and badges under the organization's brand.
Open Badges: Enterprise product page states Open Badges support. Exact version/certification role is NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED in these reviewed product documents.
W3C VC: Enterprise page explicitly lists W3C Verifiable Credentials. Exact data-model version, proof suite and interoperability require testing.
CLR: Dedicated CLR page describes creating and managing academic and non-academic learning records. Confirm standard version and certification role.
Skills: CLR page documents learning-outcome-to-skill mapping and tracking competencies.
Learner Records: CLR product spans coursework, co-curricular achievements, certifications, microcredentials and digital wallet support.
Workforce Intelligence: CLR page connects skills with industry requirements and curriculum decisions. Comparable job-market dataset coverage, licensing and refresh are NOT PUBLICLY SPECIFIED.
Verification: Training credentials have verification/sharing workflows; enterprise page describes standards-based and blockchain verification options. Test dependencies rather than assuming permanence.
Analytics: Delivery, engagement and sharing analytics across programmes.
API: Enterprise documentation describes a REST API, webhooks and a sandbox.
Integrations: Named LMS/CRM integrations and automation including Canvas, Moodle, Salesforce and Zapier; CLR page also discusses LMS/SIS integration. Confirm scope.
Security: Trust centre states ISO 27001:2022 and GDPR; training page also advertises SOC 2 Type II auditing. Request current certificates/reports and their scope; neither was independently audited here.
Data Residency: Trust centre specifies configurable Google Cloud EU (europe-west1) or US (us-east1/us-central1) regions per customer. Confirm transfers, support access and backups.
Pricing: Recipient-based public monthly/yearly options and free tier; the retrieved selector shows $750/year for 500 people. This is a selected scenario, not a universal minimum price.
Contract: Pricing FAQ describes monthly/yearly billing and multi-year enterprise agreements; enterprise page describes contractual SLA and support targets.
Higher Education: Dedicated CLR product addresses academic/co-curricular learning, institutions, LMS and SIS use cases.
Enterprise: Enterprise page lists teams/roles, SSO, API, sandbox, named support, SLA and residency options.
Certification Bodies: Partner and channel certification, resellers and technician/customer education use cases are documented; confirm a professional body's specific renewal governance.
Workforce Use Cases: Employee learning, compliance training, leadership, partner certification and skills-oriented learner records.
